The repetition is large: **2,259,794 whole reads, only 244,728 distinct** (9.2×), and 232,766 part reads with 72,322 distinct (3.2×). The pack is 454 MB now: records 168 MB, answers 269 MB. Posting the design and arithmetic before building, since this changes the shared store's format.

<to_controller>DESIGN (c), dictionary-indexed reads. Measured on the shipped std pack (`avra cache families`'s new reads line): 454 MB = records 168 + answers 269. Reads: 2,259,794 whole, 244,728 distinct (9.2× repeat); 232,766 part, 72,322 distinct (3.2×).
1. Keyed by: each pack gets a READ TABLE, the distinct (question, whole answer seen) pairs and the distinct part reads, sorted by hash and written in the pack's index. A record holds a read as its table index (a varint, ~3 B) instead of 32 B (whole) or 64 B (part). Records are still checked where they lie: an index resolves through the pack's table.
2. Also: a QUESTION TABLE of (query_name, code_hash) per pack. Each question now spells both as text; a few hundred distinct against ~300K questions.
3. Drafts: a segment interns its reads as it streams records, and the table is written at seal. ABSORB AND COMPACTION CAN'T COPY A RECORD'S OCTETS ANY MORE, since indices are per pack: a carried record is re-encoded against the new pack's table (one table lookup per read). That is the real cost of (c). Absorb gets slower in proportion to reads carried; I'd measure it on the warm-edit receipt.
4. Format: a new pack format (QUESTION_SHAPE / pack-format bump), so an old store reads as cold, never wrong.
5. Arithmetic: whole reads 72 MB → ~15 MB (dictionary 7.8 + indices ~7); part reads 15 → ~5 MB; question names/code hashes ~30 → ~1 MB. Records 168 → ~65 MB, pack 454 → ~350 MB.
**So (c) alone doesn't reach < 100 MB.** The rest is answers: lowering every std body is ~180 MB (lowered_under 51, lowered_method_under 40, body_facts 49, method_body_typed 23 of answers). Options:
- (e) ship no lowering: a dependent lowers the bodies it reaches. I can measure the cold cost first; for json the build reaches ~200 bodies;
- (d) gzip the shipped pack, ÷3.
(c)+(e) is likely ~100 MB.
Recommendation: measure (e) first (cheap: a dependents' pass without bodies_lowered, then re-time cold json and http builds). Then (c), which shrinks every store and not only the shipped one. Your call on order, and on whether (c)'s absorb cost is acceptable.</to_controller>

I've measured and written up (c), and I'm waiting for the lead's call before changing the store format.

**Measured on the shipped std pack (454 MB):** records are 168 MB and answers 269 MB.

| | Total | Distinct | Repeat |
|---|---|---|---|
| Whole reads | 2,259,794 | 244,728 | 9.2× |
| Part reads | 232,766 | 72,322 | 3.2× |

**The design I posted:**
- **Read table:** each pack keeps one table of its distinct reads, and a record stores each read as a small index into it instead of 32 or 64 bytes of hashes.
- **Question table:** the same for each question's query name and code hash.
- **The real cost:** when packs are merged or compacted, records can no longer be copied as raw bytes, because the indices belong to one pack. Each record would have to be re-encoded against the new pack's table, so merging gets slower in proportion to the reads it carries.
- **Old stores:** the format version changes, so an old store reads as cold, never wrong.

**Estimate:** records drop from 168 MB to about 65 MB, so the pack goes from 454 MB to about 350 MB. That isn't enough on its own for the 100 MB target.

Most of what's left is answers. Lowering every std body accounts for about 180 MB of them. I proposed two ways to deal with that:
- **(e)** stop shipping lowering, so a program lowers only the std bodies it actually reaches.
- **(d)** gzip the shipped pack, which shrinks the download about 3×.

My recommendation is to measure (e) first, since it's cheap to test, then build (c), which shrinks every store, not just the shipped one.

One more thing: `avra cache families` now prints a line counting total and distinct reads. It builds and is used for these numbers, but it isn't committed yet.

5. Arithmetic: whole reads 72 MB → ~15 MB (dictionary 7.8 + indices ~7); part reads 15 → ~5 MB; question names/code hashes ~30 → ~1 MB. Records 168 → ~65 MB, pack 454 → ~350 MB.
**So (c) alone doesn't reach < 100 MB.** The rest is answers: lowering every std body is ~180 MB (lowered_under 51, lowered_method_under 40, body_facts 49, method_body_typed 23 of answers). Options:
- (e) ship no lowering: a dependent lowers the bodies it reaches. I can measure the cold cost first; for json the build reaches ~200 bodies;
- (d) gzip the shipped pack, ÷3.
(c)+(e) is likely ~100 MB.
Recommendation: measure (e) first (cheap: a dependents' pass without bodies_lowered, then re-time cold json and http builds). Then (c), which shrinks every store and not only the shipped one. Your call on order, and on whether (c)'s absorb cost is acceptable.</to_controller>

I've measured and written up (c), and I'm waiting for the lead's call before changing the store format.

**Measured on the shipped std pack (454 MB):** records are 168 MB and answers 269 MB.

| | Total | Distinct | Repeat |
|---|---|---|---|
| Whole reads | 2,259,794 | 244,728 | 9.2× |
| Part reads | 232,766 | 72,322 | 3.2× |

**The design I posted:**
- **Read table:** each pack keeps one table of its distinct reads, and a record stores each read as a small index into it instead of 32 or 64 bytes of hashes.
- **Question table:** the same for each question's query name and code hash.
- **The real cost:** when packs are merged or compacted, records can no longer be copied as raw bytes, because the indices belong to one pack. Each record would have to be re-encoded against the new pack's table, so merging gets slower in proportion to the reads it carries.
- **Old stores:** the format version changes, so an old store reads as cold, never wrong.

**Estimate:** records drop from 168 MB to about 65 MB, so the pack goes from 454 MB to about 350 MB. That isn't enough on its own for the 100 MB target.

Most of what's left is answers. Lowering every std body accounts for about 180 MB of them. I proposed two ways to deal with that:
- **(e)** stop shipping lowering, so a program lowers only the std bodies it actually reaches.
- **(d)** gzip the shipped pack, which shrinks the download about 3×.

My recommendation is to measure (e) first, since it's cheap to test, then build (c), which shrinks every store, not just the shipped one.

One more thing: `avra cache families` now prints a line counting total and distinct reads. It builds and is used for these numbers, but it isn't committed yet.

<to_controller>33b1ae92 on avra-lane-defects, for batch 58. The bundle is now base55..33b1ae92, and the .md is updated.
Machine-store layering made cheap. Callgrind, store on against off, showed +504K string compares, all in map lookups: `NameSets.union` keyed each union by the text "a,b" of its ids, `set_shared` by "${id}", and `package_at` scanned every place with a string `==`. Now unions and sharing live in HashKeyedTables keyed by the ids, and places are root → package and name → served tables, with `package_at` walking up to the nearest root.
Census string compares (base55 snapshot, cold):
- check-program with the store 45,297,487 → **44,673,659**; without it, 44,658,049. The store's cost fell from +518K to +15.6K;
- check-cli 271,323,071 → **264,785,978**;
- both are now below pre-4d873bb0 (274,455,796 / 44,992,531).
Gate PASS: program, idioms, witness-b, cli. Next: (c), once 57's head arrives to merge.</to_controller>

The machine store's layering is cheap now, committed as 33b1ae92 on `avra-lane-defects` for batch 58. On check-program it costs about 15.6K extra string compares instead of 518K.

**Cause:** with the machine store on, the engine tracks which packages every answer reads, to decide which store keeps it. Three lookups in that bookkeeping compared strings every time:
- Combining two packages' read sets was looked up under the text of their two ids (`"a,b"`).
- Whether a set is shared was looked up under `"${id}"`.
- Finding a path's package scanned all ~45 package places, comparing strings each time.

**Fix:**
- The combined sets and the shared flags now sit in std-program's integer-keyed table (`HashKeyedTable`), keyed by the ids themselves. Avra's `Map` only takes text keys, so it couldn't do this.
- Package places are now two lookup tables: root to package, and package to whether the machine store serves it. A path's package is found by walking up its directories to the nearest root.

**Census string compares**, cold over the base55 snapshot:

| Workload | Before | After | Pre-4d873bb0 level |
|---|---|---|---|
| check-program, machine store on | 45,297,487 | 44,673,659 | 44,992,531 |
| check-program, machine store off | — | 44,658,049 | |
| check-cli, machine store on | 271,323,071 | 264,785,978 | 274,455,796 |

Both workloads are now below the level from before the licence check.

**Gate:** the program, idioms, witness-b and cli slices pass. The container restarted partway through; witness-b and cli were re-run afterwards and passed.

I also freed about 31 GB of disk (it was down to 10 GB) by deleting only my own measurement caches with `find -delete`.

- avra-lane-defects.md

import re,collections
def callers(f):
    # parse callgrind: count calls= lines under fn= blocks whose cfn= is avra_streq
    names={}; cur=None; cnt=collections.Counter(); pend=None
    for line in open(f, errors='replace'):
        line=line.rstrip('\n')
        m=re.match(r'^fn=\((\d+)\)(?: (.*))?$',line)
        if m:
            i,n=m.groups()
            if n: names[i]=n
            cur=names.get(i,i); continue
        m=re.match(r'^cfn=\((\d+)\)(?: (.*))?$',line)
        if m:
            i,n=m.groups()
            if n: names[i]=n
            pend=names.get(i,i); continue
        m=re.match(r'^calls=(\d+)',line)
        if m and pend=='avra_streq':
            cnt[cur]+=int(m.group(1)); pend=None
        elif m: pend=None
    return cnt

mkdir -p "$out"
find "$out" -mindepth 1 -delete
compiler=${COST_COMPILER:-build/avra.census}
if [ -z "${COST_COMPILER:-}" ]; then
    sh tools/census_compiler.sh "$compiler"
fi
[ -x "$compiler" ] || { echo "cost: no census compiler at $compiler"; exit 1; }

src=$out/src
mkdir -p "$src/build"
git archive "$snapshot" | tar -x -C "$src"
cp "$compiler" "$src/build/avra"
find build -maxdepth 1 -type f \( -name '*.o' -o -name '*.a' -o -name '*.so' -o -name 'avra_hot.bc' -o -name 'avra_hot.inc' \) \
    -exec cp {} "$src/build/" \;
printf '%s\n' "$snapshot" > "$out/snapshot"
cache=$root/$out/cache

# One run of the census compiler in the snapshot, once what it reads is older than the stamp window:
# its census to <name>.out, what it printed to <name>.stdout.
counted() {
    name=$1; shift
    sleep 3
    started=$(date +%s)
    # the census reports at exit only where the run accounts (AVRA_MEM_STATS)
    (cd "$src" && AVRA_MEM_STATS=1 AVRA_WORK_AHEAD_OFF=1 AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 AVRA_CACHE_DIR="$cache" AVRA_STORE_KEPT_HERE=1 \
        sh "$root/tools/memcap.sh" "${COST_CAP_MB:-8000}" taskset -c 0 build/avra "$@" \
        > "$root/$out/$name.stdout" 2> "$root/$out/$name.out") || {
        tail -20 "$out/$name.out"; echo "cost: $name failed ($*)"; exit 1; }
    echo "cost: $name $(($(date +%s) - started)) s"
}

# One warm findings run of the cli, its `worked:` line kept as <name>.out, its census beside it.
warm() {
    counted "$1" tapes --findings packages/cli
    mv "$out/$1.out" "$out/$1.census"
    grep '^worked: ' "$out/$1.census" > "$out/$1.out" || { echo "cost: $1 printed no worked line"; exit 1; }

#!/bin/sh
# THE CENSUS COMPILER: the cli this tree builds, over a runtime compiled with -DAVRA_CENSUS, written
# to <out>. It counts exactly what the shipping compiler does and never ships: the shipping runtime
# library is rebuilt before this answers, and the cli's own product is gone.
#   sh tools/census_compiler.sh build/avra.census
#
# THE BUILDER IS build/avra unless CENSUS_BUILDER names another: a layout rule is the BUILDING
# compiler's, so a census of a rule builds the census compiler with a compiler that has it.
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
out=${1:-build/avra.census}
builder=${CENSUS_BUILDER:-build/avra}
[ -x "$builder" ] || { echo "census: no $builder to build the census compiler with — run \`make avra\` first"; exit 1; }
# A MADE BOX IS NAMED BY ITS CALLER'S CALLER, two frames up, which only frame pointers reach:
# macOS keeps them always, Linux only when asked, in the runtime and in every emitted fn.
counted="-DAVRA_CENSUS -fno-omit-frame-pointer"
shipping() {
    make --no-print-directory build/libavra_runtime.a > /dev/null 2>&1 || \
        echo "census: the shipping runtime did NOT rebuild — run \`make build/libavra_runtime.a\`"
    find packages/cli/src/main packages/cli/src/main.av.ll -maxdepth 0 -delete 2> /dev/null || :
}
trap shipping EXIT INT TERM
make --no-print-directory CFLAGS_avra_runtime="$counted" CFLAGS_avra_hot="$counted" build/libavra_runtime.a > /dev/null
# THE COUNTED LEAVES STAY CALLS: the bitcode the compiler inlines was
# built without the census, so an inlined retain would count nothing.
# THE MINTED BOXES ARE NAMED: each box a runtime row makes is counted by
# its type (AVRA_CENSUS_TYPES), the `type:` table.
# THE CENSUS COUNTS THE COMPILER'S OWN WORK: the old path's check the net runs first is not that work.
AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 AVRA_FRAME_POINTERS=1 AVRA_INLINE_RUNTIME=0 AVRA_CENSUS_TYPES=1 AVRA_PROGRAM_MODE=release \
    "$builder" build packages/cli > build/census-build.out 2>&1 || {

#!/bin/sh
# THE EXACT-COUNT GATE'S MEASUREMENT: the census compiler of this tree, run over FIXED workloads whose
# sources are one pinned commit (the `snapshot` row of tools/cost.baseline): cold, each run's census
# kept as build/cost/<workload>.out; and warm after each edit of a fixed set, the answers it worked out
# again kept as build/cost/edit-<kind>.out. tools/cost_ratchet.py judges them.
#   sh tools/cost.sh                      the baseline's snapshot
#   COST_SNAPSHOT=<sha> sh tools/cost.sh  another snapshot (what `make cost-accept` records)
#   COST_COMPILER=<file> sh tools/cost.sh a census compiler already built from this tree
#
# A FIXED INPUT MEASURES THE COMPILER: the snapshot is exported whole, std included, and the census
# compiler stands at its build/avra beside the objects a build links, so every package it reads is
# the snapshot's.
# ONE PROCESS ON ONE CORE DOES ALL THE WORK: a forked worker's counts are its own, so no body is
# lowered ahead (AVRA_WORK_AHEAD_OFF) and the run is held to one core (`taskset`), the width every
# emitter reads, so objects are made in this process by one worker.
# EVERY COLD RUN STARTS BARE: an empty store, and no product a run before it left, which a build reads.
# A FILE IS READ ONLY ONCE IT IS OLDER THAN THE STAMP WINDOW (io.stamp withholds a stamp from a path
# changed in the last two seconds), so what a run stamps never depends on how fast it began.
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
root=$(pwd)
out=build/cost
snapshot=${COST_SNAPSHOT:-$(awk '$1 == "snapshot" { print $2 }' tools/cost.baseline 2> /dev/null)}
[ -n "$snapshot" ] || { echo "cost: tools/cost.baseline names no snapshot"; exit 1; }
# A SHALLOW CLONE FETCHES THE ONE COMMIT IT PINS.
git cat-file -e "$snapshot^{commit}" 2> /dev/null || git fetch -q --depth=1 origin "$snapshot" 2> /dev/null || :
git cat-file -e "$snapshot^{commit}" 2> /dev/null || {
    echo "cost: snapshot $snapshot is not in this clone and could not be fetched"; exit 1; }
command -v taskset > /dev/null || { echo "cost: no taskset to hold the run to one core"; exit 1; }

# The cold workloads: a name, then the command the census compiler runs in the snapshot.
workloads() {
    cat << 'EOF'
check-cli check --counts packages/cli
build-cli build packages/cli
check-program check --counts packages/std-program
EOF
}

# THE WARM RE-RUN WORK OF AN EDIT: over the store the cold cli check left, `tapes --findings` of the
# cli is settled; then each edit of one file is made, the findings run warm and the answers it worked
# out again kept (its `worked:` line), and the file put back and the findings warmed back, so each edit
# meets the store the one before it left. The edits and their file are the warm lane's measured
# table's, so a row reads against its design budget.
# kind|text|what it becomes, `\n` between lines; a noop edits nothing.
edited=packages/cli/src/commands/cache.av
edits() {
    cat << 'EOF'
noop||
inline|//! in, its own verbs. The store is a directory of immutable packs, each the|//! in, its own verbs. The store is a folder of immutable packs, each the
literal|    println("avra cache clean: ${compacted_said(dir)}")|    println("avra cache cleaned: ${compacted_said(dir)}")
comment|    let shared? = machine_layer() else { return 0 }|    // a note\n    let shared? = machine_layer() else { return 0 }
body|    let shared? = machine_layer() else { return 0 }|    let shared? = machine_layer() else { return 0 }\n    let _ = cache_dir().length
signature|fn octets_of(packs: List<PackListed>) -> int {|fn octets_of(packs: List<PackListed>, most: int = 0) -> int {
added|fn cache_dir() -> string {|fn cache_unused() -> int { 3 }\n\nfn cache_dir() -> string {
added_after|fn octets_of(packs: List<PackListed>) -> int { packs.fold(0, (sum, p) -> sum + p.octets) }|fn octets_of(packs: List<PackListed>) -> int { packs.fold(0, (sum, p) -> sum + p.octets) }\n\nfn spare_one() -> int { 1 }
EOF
}

mkdir -p "$out"

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""THE EXACT-COUNT GATE: what the compiler DOES on fixed workloads, counted by the census runtime.

    cost_ratchet.py --judge <dir>      judge a `tools/cost.sh` run against tools/cost.baseline
    cost_ratchet.py --accept <dir>     record a run: rows fall to what it measured; a run over another
                                       snapshot records that snapshot and every row as measured
    cost_ratchet.py --edit <file> <kind> <text> <becomes>
                                       make one edit of tools/cost.sh's set: the text, which stands in
                                       the file once, becomes what follows (`\\n` a line break); a
                                       `rename` renames the word through the file
    cost_ratchet.py --self-test

`tools/cost.sh` runs the census compiler of the tree cold over workloads whose sources are ONE pinned
commit (the baseline's `snapshot` row), so a count moves only when the compiler's work does; and warm
after each of a fixed set of edits, where the count is the queries worked out again (an `edit-<kind>`
row), so a change that trades warm work for cold is seen. Counts are exact and machine-independent:
the runtime counts operations, never time.

A COUNTER OVER ITS ROW BY MORE THAN THE TOLERANCE FAILS, naming the workload, the counter and both
numbers. A counter under its row stays until `make cost-accept` lowers it; an accept never raises a
row over the same snapshot. Moving the snapshot is an accept with `COST_SNAPSHOT=<sha>`, which records
the new commit and every count it measured. A run that printed no count for a row FAILS.
"""
import os
import re
import sys

import ratchet_rows as rows_lib

BASELINE = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "cost.baseline")
TOLERANCE_PPM = 500
HEAD = """\
# THE EXACT-COUNT BASELINE: what the census compiler does, cold, on each fixed workload of the pinned
# snapshot (`make cost`, tools/cost.sh, tools/cost_ratchet.py). Exact and machine-independent. A row
# more than 0.05% over FAILS the gate; a row only falls, through `make cost-accept`; a new snapshot is
# `COST_SNAPSHOT=<sha> make cost-accept`, which records the commit and every count.
"""
# Each census line the runtime prints at exit, and the counters it carries, in order.
PRINTED = (
    (r"rc: (\d+) retains, (\d+) releases, (\d+) reclaims", ("retains", "releases", "reclaims")),
639:    avra_say("rc: %lld copies, %lld string compares\n", (long long)g_copies, (long long)g_streqs);

# THE GATE, IN SLICES: every receipt a landing is held to, cut into slices that each run alone in a
# tree of their own, so N machines run N slices at once and the gate takes as long as its longest
# slice. A slice builds the compiler of HEAD itself when build/avra was built from anything else,
# runs every row on the program layer, the net off but where a row's claim is the net, empties the
# stores a cold row reads, bounds every command, keeps each row's words under build/gate/<slice>/, and
# ends with ONE line:
#   GATE <slice> <sha8> PASS|FAIL rows=<n> failed=<n> <seconds>s
# exiting 0 on PASS, 1 on FAIL.
#
#   sh tools/gate.sh list               each slice, one a line, with what it holds
#   sh tools/gate.sh <slice> [arg]      one slice; the idioms slices take the base sha their diff starts at
#   sh tools/gate.sh seed               build/gate/compiler-<sha8>.tar.gz: HEAD's compiler — ONE generation, built
#                                       here first where none of HEAD's stands — and every object a tree
#                                       links with; `pack` is its other name. Run it once; every slice
#                                       then starts from `unpack` and builds nothing.
#   sh tools/gate.sh unpack <file>      seeds this tree from a pack, and holds its stamp to HEAD's: a
#                                       seeded slice builds no compiler
#
# A test row runs every suite (AVRA_SUITE_ALL=1), so it names every failing case, never only the first.
#
# GATE_OLD_PATH=0 drops every row that compares against the old path (they read AVRA_PROGRAM=0);
# when the old path goes, its default goes to 0 and those rows go with one line each.
set -u
root=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
cd "$root" || exit 1
unset AVRA_PROGRAM AVRA_PROGRAM_MODE
export AVRA_SUITE_ALL=1
# THE NET IS OFF unless a row's claim is the net: the old path's check before every program-layer
# compile doubles what each row costs and proves nothing a row here asks of it. The rows that keep it
# (AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=1) are the ones that count what it says: the build slice's net-on cli builds and
# their "program-layer false refusal" count, the findings slices' build of every package, held to that
# same count, and the cli's suite, which holds the words a user meets through a child build/avra (at
# slice_cli). `tapes --findings` passes no door, so the net never stood in it.
export AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0

OLD_PATH=${GATE_OLD_PATH:-1}
# the bound of one row, and of a compiler build
ROW_SECS=${GATE_ROW_SECS:-2400}
# every `test` row's failing NAMES are held to tools/gate/<package>.names, the cases a sandbox fails
# the packages whose tests the doors slices run
DOORS_A="std-json std-task std-validate std-text std-sql std-queue std-time"
DOORS_B="std-ui std-http"

slices() {
    cat <<'EOF'
build      make try; make avra twice, the second cold, the two binaries one; cli build cold+warm, net on and off, 0 false refusals
avrac-a    test packages/std-avrac — half of src/compiler/tests, dealt in turn, and every dir of src/compiler but tests and soundness
avrac-g    test packages/std-avrac — the other half of src/compiler/tests, and src/compiler/soundness
avrac-b    test packages/std-avrac — src/features/[a-e]*
avrac-c    test packages/std-avrac — src/features/[f-m]*
avrac-d    test packages/std-avrac — src/features/[n-r]*
avrac-e    test packages/std-avrac — src/features/[s-z]*
avrac-f    test packages/std-avrac — src/features' own files, and every dir of src/ but compiler and features
cli        test packages/cli, its failing names held to tools/gate/cli.names
program    test packages/std-program and std-relation; make runtime-tests, rt-header and rt-ns: every runtime row's C body and typed method
idioms-avrac  check --baseline tools/idioms.baseline on std-avrac, when the diff from <base> touches it
idioms-cli    the same on cli
idioms     the same on every other package the diff from <base> touches
fmt        fmt --check on every .av the diff from <base> changes (tools/fmt_changed.sh); <base> is the program landed last, never a batch's own base
sound      AVRA_SOUND_CHECK=1 check packages/cli, the memory pass's proof run over the program, 0 defects; AVRA_VERIFY_LLVM=1 build packages/cli, every emitted fn verified
cost       make cost: the census compiler, cold, over tools/cost.baseline's snapshot; every count within 0.05% of its row
doors-a    test std-json std-task std-validate std-text std-sql std-queue std-time
doors-b    test std-ui std-http; make ui-host-test and ui-host, std-ui's program tests built and run
findings-a tapes --findings on std-avrac and cli, 0 refusals; std-avrac built, 0 program-layer false refusals
findings-b the same on a third of every other package, dealt in turn
findings-c the next third
findings-d the last third
refusal-a  witness_program_refusal over a third of its cases, dealt in turn
refusal-b  the next third
refusal-c  the last third
witness-b  witness_program_runs, heir_save_attack, share_merge_attack, wave_share_attack, beside_attack, _ledger, _suites, _doors; witness_program_differential; make flow-trace; witness_compiler_key; docs_cache_attack, obj_gone_attack, moved_tree_attack, layer_sites_attack, closure_gather_attack, store_bound_attack, path_leak_attack, case_leftover_attack, witness_program_fixes, root_listing_attack, two_compilers_attack, flow_trace_swap_attack, std_answers_attack
warnings-a witness_program_warnings — the cli built cold and again with no change, on both paths
warnings-b witness_program_warnings — the cli's check on both paths, and the cases under tools/program-warnings/
warnings-c witness_program_warnings — the cli edited, built warm on the program layer
edit-a     witness_program_edit, WITNESS_ONLY="embed infer composed gathered"
edit-b     witness_program_edit, WITNESS_ONLY=1
edit-c     witness_program_edit, WITNESS_ONLY=5
edit-d     witness_program_edit, WITNESS_ONLY=10
edit-e     witness_program_edit, WITNESS_ONLY=rename
edit-f     witness_program_edit, WITNESS_ONLY=modes-whole
edit-g     witness_program_edit, WITNESS_ONLY=modes-layered
EOF
}

# whether build/avra was built from this tree's compiler source: the stamp's hash of that source, the
# commit it stood at aside — a commit that moves no compiler source moves no compiler
compiler_stands() {
    [ -x build/avra ] && [ "$(cut -d' ' -f1 build/.avra-built-from 2>/dev/null)" = "$(sh tools/work built-from . | cut -d' ' -f1)" ]
}

# what a built tree holds that a fresh one needs to stand as built: the compiler, its hot leaves, its
# stamp, and every object, archive, library, content stamp and dependency list build/ keeps at its top
packed() {
    for f in build/avra build/avra_hot.bc build/avra_hot.inc build/.avra-built-from; do [ ! -f "$f" ] || echo "$f"; done
    find build -maxdepth 1 -type f \( -name '*.o' -o -name '*.a' -o -name '*.so' -o -name '*.sha' -o -name '*.d' \) | sort
}

# a tree seeded from the pack `$1`, or left as it was: a pack is proved whole first — gzip's own check,
# a listing to its end, the compiler and its stamp in it — and refused when its stamp is not this
# tree's compiler source; then laid down in a staging directory and moved into build/ only once every
# file is out, so a truncated pack never seeds half a tree. Every file moved is touched to one instant,
# so make finds no object older than its own stamp — the content stamps decide what moved.
unpacked() {
    [ -f "${1:-}" ] || { echo "gate: unpack names a pack — sh tools/gate.sh unpack <file>" >&2; exit 2; }
    pack=$(cd "$(dirname "$1")" && pwd)/$(basename "$1")
    refused() { echo "gate: $(basename "$pack") $1 — not seeded" >&2; exit 1; }
    gzip -t "$pack" 2>/dev/null || refused "is not whole (gzip -t)"
    list=$(tar -tzf "$pack" 2>/dev/null) || refused "does not list to its end"
    for f in build/avra build/.avra-built-from; do printf '%s\n' "$list" | grep -qx "$f" || refused "holds no $f"; done
    packed_hash=$(tar -xzOf "$pack" build/.avra-built-from | cut -d' ' -f1)
    tree_hash=$(sh tools/work built-from . | cut -d' ' -f1)
    [ "$packed_hash" = "$tree_hash" ] || refused "was built from compiler source $packed_hash, this tree's is $tree_hash"
    stage=build/gate/unpacking
    mkdir -p build/gate
    [ ! -e "$stage" ] || find "$stage" -delete
    mkdir -p "$stage"
    if ! tar -xzf "$pack" -C "$stage"; then find "$stage" -delete; refused "did not extract"; fi
    touch build/gate/.unpacked
    printf '%s\n' "$list" | while IFS= read -r f; do
        [ -f "$stage/$f" ] || continue
        touch -r build/gate/.unpacked "$stage/$f"
        mv -f "$stage/$f" "$f"
    done
    find "$stage" -delete
    compiler_stands || { echo "gate: build/avra does not stand as HEAD's compiler after the unpack" >&2; exit 1; }
    echo "gate: seeded from $(basename "$pack") — build/avra stands as HEAD's compiler"
    exit 0
}

[ $# -ge 1 ] || { echo "gate: name a slice, or \`list\`" >&2; exit 2; }
slice=$1
shift
if [ "$slice" = list ]; then slices; exit 0; fi
if [ "$slice" = unpack ]; then unpacked "$@"; fi
[ "$slice" = seed ] && slice=pack
[ "$slice" = pack ] || slices | awk '{ print $1 }' | grep -qx "$slice" || { echo "gate: no slice \`$slice\` — \`sh tools/gate.sh list\` names them" >&2; exit 2; }

sha8=$(git rev-parse --short=8 HEAD)
out="$root/build/gate/$slice"
mkdir -p "$out"
find "$out" -mindepth 1 -delete
export AVRA_CACHE_DIR="$out/machine"
# a slice copies, counts and empties stores between builds, so each build saves its own before it
# answers; the build slice's timing rows alone leave the save to an heir, as a user's build does
export AVRA_STORE_KEPT_HERE=1
mkdir -p "$AVRA_CACHE_DIR"
began=$(date +%s)
rows=0
failed=0
failures=""

# one row: `$1` its name, the rest its command, bounded; its words at $out/<name>.log
row() {
    name=$1; shift
    rows=$((rows + 1))
    t0=$(date +%s)
    if sh tools/bounded.sh "$ROW_SECS" "$@" >"$out/$name.log" 2>&1; then
        echo "row $name pass $(( $(date +%s) - t0 ))s" >>"$out/rows"
        return 0
    fi
    failed=$((failed + 1))
    failures="$failures $name"
    echo "row $name FAIL $(( $(date +%s) - t0 ))s" >>"$out/rows"
    return 1
}

# a row that judges what an earlier row left: `$1` its name, `$2` the verdict (0 holds)
judged() {
    rows=$((rows + 1))
    if [ "$2" = 0 ]; then echo "row $1 pass" >>"$out/rows"; return 0; fi
    failed=$((failed + 1))
    failures="$failures $1"
    echo "row $1 FAIL" >>"$out/rows"
    return 1
}

# a row that compares against the old path: run only while the old path stands
old_row() { [ "$OLD_PATH" = 1 ] || return 0; row "$@"; }

# every store under the packages named emptied — a nested package's and a program test's too — so the
# rows after read them cold
cold() { for p in "$@"; do find "packages/$p" -name .avra-cache -prune -exec find {} -delete \; ; done; return 0; }

# build/avra as HEAD's compiler: kept when it was built from this tree's compiler source, else made in
# ONE generation — from the committed seed's link where no compiler stands, else from the one that does
# — with the package libraries beside it, built without building the compiler again. A gate's
# compiler makes no claim of the net, so it is built without it; the two-generation fixed point is the
# build slice's.
compiler() {
    if compiler_stands; then return 0; fi
    if [ ! -x build/avra ]; then row compiler-recover make recover || return 1; fi
    row compiler-gen1 env AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 make avra || return 1
    row compiler-libs env AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 make -o avra libs
}

# what `$1`'s cold build of packages/cli took, in seconds, net on or off by `$2`
cli_built() {
    cold cli
    find "$AVRA_CACHE_DIR" -mindepth 1 -delete
    c0=$(date +%s)
    row "cli-build-$1-cold" env -u AVRA_STORE_KEPT_HERE AVRA_PROGRAM_NET="$2" build/avra build packages/cli || return 1
    c1=$(date +%s)
    row "cli-build-$1-warm" env -u AVRA_STORE_KEPT_HERE AVRA_PROGRAM_NET="$2" build/avra build packages/cli || return 1
    echo "cli build net $1: cold $((c1 - c0))s, warm $(( $(date +%s) - c1 ))s" >>"$out/seconds"
    # the warm build's heir waited out, before a row after empties the store it saves
    env AVRA_PROGRAM_NET="$2" build/avra build packages/cli >/dev/null 2>&1 || :
}

slice_build() {
    row try make try
    row avra-a make avra && cp build/avra "$out/avra-a"
    cold cli
    row avra-b make avra && { cmp -s build/avra "$out/avra-a"; judged fixed-point $?; }
    cli_built on 1
    cli_built off 0
    judged cli-build-false-refusals "$(cat "$out"/cli-build-*.log | grep -c 'program-layer false refusal')"
}

# the std-avrac suite over `$@`, its paths under the package: one row for every path of std-avrac's
# own, and a row each for a path that is a package of its own nested in it, which `test` proves apart
avrac() {
    cold std-avrac
    own=""
    for p in "$@"; do
        if [ -f "$p/avra.toml" ]; then tested "std-avrac-$(basename "$p")" "$p"; else own="$own $p"; fi
    done
    [ -z "$own" ] || tested std-avrac $own
}
# half of std-avrac's src/compiler/tests, the `$1`-th (from 0), dealt in turn
compiler_tests_half() { find packages/std-avrac/src/compiler/tests -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 ! -name '.*' | sort | dealt "$1" 2; }
slice_avrac_a() {
    avrac $(
        {
            compiler_tests_half 0
            find packages/std-avrac/src/compiler -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 ! -name tests ! -name soundness ! -name '.*'
        } | sort
    )
}
slice_avrac_g() { avrac $({ compiler_tests_half 1; echo packages/std-avrac/src/compiler/soundness; } | sort); }
slice_avrac_b() { avrac $(find packages/std-avrac/src/features -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -type d -name '[a-e]*' | sort); }
slice_avrac_c() { avrac $(find packages/std-avrac/src/features -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -type d -name '[f-m]*' | sort); }
slice_avrac_d() { avrac $(find packages/std-avrac/src/features -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -type d -name '[n-r]*' | sort); }
slice_avrac_e() { avrac $(find packages/std-avrac/src/features -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -type d -name '[s-z]*' | sort); }
slice_avrac_f() {
    avrac $(
        {
            find packages/std-avrac/src/features -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -name '*.av'
            find packages/std-avrac/src -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 ! -name compiler ! -name features ! -name '.*'
        } | sort
    )
}

# the words on its lines that `dealt k n` keeps: every n-th, starting at the k-th (from 0), so a
# list's parts share its weight in turn
dealt() { awk -v k="$1" -v n="$2" '(NR - 1) % n == k'; }

# `test` over `$2…` as the row `$1`, judged by the NAMES that fail: each must be one
# tools/gate/<package>.names pins (a case a sandbox's environment fails — root writes any directory, no
# terminal, no network), never a count. With no pin file, every failure fails the row.
# A CASE THAT ENDS THE SUITE'S PROCESS (`avra: while running <case>`) fails no case by name and leaves
# every case after it unrun, so it is never passed over: each must be one tools/gate/<package>.traps
# lists, by the first line the runner says it under.
tested() {
    name=$1; shift
    pkg=$(echo "$1" | cut -d/ -f2)
    sh tools/bounded.sh "$ROW_SECS" build/avra test "$@" >"$out/$name.log" 2>&1
    ran=$?
    grep '^    ✗' "$out/$name.log" | sed 's/ @ .*//; s/^    ✗ //' | sort -u >"$out/$name.failed"
    listed "tools/gate/$pkg.names" >"$out/$name.known"
    comm -23 "$out/$name.failed" "$out/$name.known" >"$out/$name.unpinned"
    grep '^avra: while running ' "$out/$name.log" | sed 's/ @ .*//; s/^avra: while running //' | sort -u >"$out/$name.trapped"
    listed "tools/gate/$pkg.traps" >"$out/$name.traps"
    comm -23 "$out/$name.trapped" "$out/$name.traps" >"$out/$name.untrapped"
    if [ -s "$out/$name.untrapped" ]; then judged "$name" "$(wc -l <"$out/$name.untrapped" | tr -d ' ')"; return; fi
    # a run that fails no case and ends none must have exited clean; one that fails only pinned cases
    # or ends at a listed one stopped on them
    if [ ! -s "$out/$name.failed" ] && [ ! -s "$out/$name.trapped" ]; then judged "$name" "$ran"; return; fi
    judged "$name" "$(wc -l <"$out/$name.unpinned" | tr -d ' ')"
}

# the lines the pin file `$1` lists, sorted, each once; none where there is no such file
listed() { if [ -f "$1" ]; then grep -v '^#' "$1" | sort -u; fi; }

# THE CLI'S SUITE RUNS WITH THE NET: its cases run build/avra as a user does and hold the words a user
# meets, refusals among them, and where the program layer accepts a program the old path refuses, those
# words are the net's — so the suite holds the shipped default, the net on. The one suite that runs the
# compiler as a child; every other test row holds what it runs in-process.
slice_cli() {
    cold cli
    export AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=1
    children_kept tested cli-suite packages/cli
    export AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0
    children_of_failed cli-suite
}

# A SUITE WHOSE CASES RUN THE COMPILER AS A CHILD KEEPS WHAT EACH CHILD DID: `$@` with every child
# `<tree>/avra` filed under $out/children/<case> by tools/gate/child_kept.sh — its arguments, its
# streams and its exit — so a red row has the words its children said.
children_kept() {
    find "$out/children" -delete 2>/dev/null || :
    export AVRA_BIN="$root/tools/gate/child_kept.sh" AVRA_CHILD_BIN="$root/build/avra" AVRA_CHILDREN="$out/children"
    "$@"
    unset AVRA_BIN AVRA_CHILD_BIN AVRA_CHILDREN
}

# the children of the cases row `$1` failed, kept; every other case's dropped
children_of_failed() {
    for d in "$out"/children/*/; do
        [ -f "$d/case" ] || continue
        grep -qxF "$(sed 's/ @ .*//' "$d/case")" "$out/$1.failed" || find "$d" -delete
    done
}

slice_program() {
    cold std-program std-relation
    tested std-program packages/std-program
    tested std-relation packages/std-relation
    row runtime-tests make runtime-tests
    # THE ROWS' CLAIMS, generated from rt_sigs(): the C header and the typed methods. A row added without
    # its regeneration is refused here, never left for the next lane to find.
    row rt-header make rt-header
    row rt-ns make rt-ns
}

# each package the diff from the base sha `$1` touches, whose name the pattern `$3` matches (`$2` keep)
# or doesn't (`$2` drop), checked against the baseline
idioms_on() {
    [ -n "${1:-}" ] || { echo "gate: $slice needs the base sha its diff starts at" >&2; exit 2; }
    if [ "$2" = drop ]; then pick=-vxE; else pick=-xE; fi
    for p in $(git diff --name-only "$1" HEAD -- packages | cut -d/ -f2 | sort -u | grep $pick "$3"); do
        [ -d "packages/$p/src" ] || continue
        cold "$p"
        row "idioms-$p" build/avra check "packages/$p" --baseline tools/idioms.baseline
    done
}

# every `.av` the diff from the base sha `$1` changes, canonical as the tree's own compiler prints it.
# The base is the program landed last: a batch gated against its own base would hold none of what
# its lanes wrote to the printer's word
fmt_on() {
    [ -n "${1:-}" ] || { echo "gate: $slice needs the base sha its diff starts at — the program landed last" >&2; exit 2; }
    row fmt-changed env AVRA=build/avra sh tools/fmt_changed.sh "$1" HEAD
}

slice_sound() {
    row sound-check-run env AVRA_SOUND_CHECK=1 build/avra check packages/cli
    cold cli
    row llvm-verified-build env AVRA_VERIFY_LLVM=1 build/avra build packages/cli
    judged sound-check-defects "$(grep -c 'language.defect' "$out/sound-check-run.log")"
}

# the census compiler builds from build/avra, the compiler this slice stands on
slice_cost() { row cost env CENSUS_BUILDER=build/avra make -s -o avra cost; }

doors() { for p in "$@"; do cold "$p"; tested "test-$p" "packages/$p"; done; }
slice_doors_a() { doors $DOORS_A; }
slice_doors_b() {
    doors $DOORS_B
    row ui-host-test make -s -o avra ui-host-test
    row ui-host make -s -o avra ui-host
}

# each package named: tapes --findings with no refusal; built — a library stops at "declares no entry
# point", which is no refusal — with no program-layer false refusal; the cli's builds are the build slice's
findings_on() {
    for p in "$@"; do
        cold "$p"
        row "findings-$p" build/avra tapes "$root/packages/$p" --findings
        judged "refusals-$p" "$(grep -c '^error\[' "$out/findings-$p.log")"
        [ "$p" != cli ] || continue
        sh tools/bounded.sh "$ROW_SECS" env AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=1 build/avra build "packages/$p" >"$out/build-$p.log" 2>&1
        judged "false-refusals-$p" "$(grep -c 'program-layer false refusal' "$out/build-$p.log")"
    done
}
HEAVY_FINDINGS="std-avrac cli"
slice_findings_a() { findings_on $HEAVY_FINDINGS; }
# a third of every other package, the `$1`-th (from 0)
findings_third() {
    findings_on $(for d in packages/*/src; do basename "$(dirname "$d")"; done | grep -vxE "$(echo $HEAVY_FINDINGS | tr ' ' '|')" | dealt "$1" 3)
}

# the refusal witness over a third of its cases — each a package (tools/lib/cases.sh) — the `$1`-th (from 0)
refusal_third() {
    old_row refusal-witness sh tools/witness_program_refusal.sh build/avra $(sh tools/witness_program_refusal.sh --cases | dealt "$1" 3)
}

slice_witness_b() {
    row runs-witness sh tools/witness_program_runs.sh build/avra
    row heir-save-attack env HEIR_ATTACK_AVRA="$root/build/avra" sh tools/heir_save_attack.sh
    row share-merge-attack env SHARE_ATTACK_AVRA="$root/build/avra" sh tools/share_merge_attack.sh
    row beside-attack env BESIDE_ATTACK_AVRA="$root/build/avra" sh tools/beside_attack.sh
    row wave-share-attack env WAVE_ATTACK_AVRA="$root/build/avra" sh tools/wave_share_attack.sh
    row flow-trace make -s -o avra flow-trace
    row compiler-key sh tools/witness_compiler_key.sh build/avra
    row docs-cache-attack sh tools/docs_cache_attack.sh
    row obj-gone-attack sh tools/obj_gone_attack.sh
    row moved-tree-attack sh tools/moved_tree_attack.sh
    row layer-sites-attack sh tools/layer_sites_attack.sh
    row closure-gather-attack sh tools/closure_gather_attack.sh
    row store-bound-attack sh tools/store_bound_attack.sh
    row path-leak-attack sh tools/path_leak_attack.sh
    row case-leftover-attack sh tools/case_leftover_attack.sh
    old_row fixes-witness sh tools/witness_program_fixes.sh build/avra
    row root-listing-attack sh tools/root_listing_attack.sh
    row two-compilers-attack sh tools/two_compilers_attack.sh
    row flow-trace-swap-attack sh tools/flow_trace_swap_attack.sh
    row std-answers-attack sh tools/std_answers_attack.sh build/avra
    row carried-store-attack env CARRIED_ATTACK_AVRA="$root/build/avra" sh tools/carried_store_attack.sh
    old_row ledger-witness sh tools/witness_program_ledger.sh build/avra
    old_row suites-witness sh tools/witness_program_suites.sh build/avra
    old_row doors-witness sh tools/witness_program_doors.sh build/avra
    old_row differential-witness sh tools/witness_program_differential.sh build/avra
}

# the warnings witness's part `$1`
warnings_part() { old_row warnings-witness env WITNESS_ONLY="$1" sh tools/witness_program_warnings.sh build/avra; }

# the edit witness's edits `$1`
edit_part() { row edit-witness env WITNESS_ONLY="$1" sh tools/witness_program_edit.sh build/avra; }

if compiler; then
    case $slice in
        pack)
            tarball="build/gate/compiler-$sha8.tar.gz"
            packed >"$out/files"
            row pack tar -czf "$tarball" -T "$out/files" && echo "pack: $tarball, $(wc -l <"$out/files" | tr -d ' ') files, $(du -k "$tarball" | cut -f1) KB" >>"$out/rows"
            ;;
        build) slice_build ;;
        avrac-a) slice_avrac_a ;;
        avrac-b) slice_avrac_b ;;
        avrac-c) slice_avrac_c ;;
        avrac-g) slice_avrac_g ;;
        avrac-d) slice_avrac_d ;;
        avrac-e) slice_avrac_e ;;
        avrac-f) slice_avrac_f ;;

        idioms-cli) idioms_on "${1:-}" keep cli ;;
        idioms) idioms_on "${1:-}" drop 'std-avrac|cli' ;;

        sound) slice_sound ;;

        doors-a) slice_doors_a ;;

fi

#!/bin/sh
# THE GATE, IN SLICES: every receipt a landing is held to, cut into slices that each run alone in a
# tree of their own, so N machines run N slices at once and the gate takes as long as its longest
# slice. A slice builds the compiler of HEAD itself when build/avra was built from anything else,
# runs every row on the program layer, the net off but where a row's claim is the net, empties the
# stores a cold row reads, bounds every command, keeps each row's words under build/gate/<slice>/, and
# ends with ONE line:
#   GATE <slice> <sha8> PASS|FAIL rows=<n> failed=<n> <seconds>s
# exiting 0 on PASS, 1 on FAIL.
#
#   sh tools/gate.sh list               each slice, one a line, with what it holds
#   sh tools/gate.sh <slice> [arg]      one slice; the idioms slices take the base sha their diff starts at
#   sh tools/gate.sh seed               build/gate/compiler-<sha8>.tar.gz: HEAD's compiler — ONE generation, built
#                                       here first where none of HEAD's stands — and every object a tree
#                                       links with; `pack` is its other name. Run it once; every slice
#                                       then starts from `unpack` and builds nothing.
#   sh tools/gate.sh unpack <file>      seeds this tree from a pack, and holds its stamp to HEAD's: a
#                                       seeded slice builds no compiler
#
# A test row runs every suite (AVRA_SUITE_ALL=1), so it names every failing case, never only the first.
#
# GATE_OLD_PATH=0 drops every row that compares against the old path (they read AVRA_PROGRAM=0);
# when the old path goes, its default goes to 0 and those rows go with one line each.
set -u
root=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
cd "$root" || exit 1
unset AVRA_PROGRAM AVRA_PROGRAM_MODE
export AVRA_SUITE_ALL=1
# THE NET IS OFF unless a row's claim is the net: the old path's check before every program-layer
# compile doubles what each row costs and proves nothing a row here asks of it. The rows that keep it
# (AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=1) are the ones that count what it says: the build slice's net-on cli builds and
# their "program-layer false refusal" count, the findings slices' build of every package, held to that
# same count, and the cli's suite, which holds the words a user meets through a child build/avra (at
# slice_cli). `tapes --findings` passes no door, so the net never stood in it.
export AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0

OLD_PATH=${GATE_OLD_PATH:-1}
# the bound of one row, and of a compiler build
ROW_SECS=${GATE_ROW_SECS:-2400}
# every `test` row's failing NAMES are held to tools/gate/<package>.names, the cases a sandbox fails
# the packages whose tests the doors slices run
DOORS_A="std-json std-task std-validate std-text std-sql std-queue std-time"
DOORS_B="std-ui std-http"

slices() {
    cat <<'EOF'
build      make try; make avra twice, the second cold, the two binaries one; cli build cold+warm, net on and off, 0 false refusals
avrac-a    test packages/std-avrac — half of src/compiler/tests, dealt in turn, and every dir of src/compiler but tests and soundness
avrac-g    test packages/std-avrac — the other half of src/compiler/tests, and src/compiler/soundness
avrac-b    test packages/std-avrac — src/features/[a-e]*
avrac-c    test packages/std-avrac — src/features/[f-m]*
avrac-d    test packages/std-avrac — src/features/[n-r]*
avrac-e    test packages/std-avrac — src/features/[s-z]*
avrac-f    test packages/std-avrac — src/features' own files, and every dir of src/ but compiler and features
cli        test packages/cli, its failing names held to tools/gate/cli.names
program    test packages/std-program and std-relation; make runtime-tests, rt-header and rt-ns: every runtime row's C body and typed method
idioms-avrac  check --baseline tools/idioms.baseline on std-avrac, when the diff from <base> touches it
idioms-cli    the same on cli
idioms     the same on every other package the diff from <base> touches
fmt        fmt --check on every .av the diff from <base> changes (tools/fmt_changed.sh); <base> is the program landed last, never a batch's own base
sound      AVRA_SOUND_CHECK=1 check packages/cli, the memory pass's proof run over the program, 0 defects; AVRA_VERIFY_LLVM=1 build packages/cli, every emitted fn verified
cost       make cost: the census compiler, cold, over tools/cost.baseline's snapshot; every count within 0.05% of its row
doors-a    test std-json std-task std-validate std-text std-sql std-queue std-time
doors-b    test std-ui std-http; make ui-host-test and ui-host, std-ui's program tests built and run
findings-a tapes --findings on std-avrac and cli, 0 refusals; std-avrac built, 0 program-layer false refusals
findings-b the same on a third of every other package, dealt in turn
findings-c the next third
findings-d the last third
refusal-a  witness_program_refusal over a third of its cases, dealt in turn
refusal-b  the next third
refusal-c  the last third
witness-b  witness_program_runs, heir_save_attack, share_merge_attack, wave_share_attack, beside_attack, _ledger, _suites, _doors; witness_program_differential; make flow-trace; witness_compiler_key; docs_cache_attack, obj_gone_attack, moved_tree_attack, layer_sites_attack, closure_gather_attack, store_bound_attack, path_leak_attack, case_leftover_attack, witness_program_fixes, root_listing_attack, two_compilers_attack, flow_trace_swap_attack, std_answers_attack
warnings-a witness_program_warnings — the cli built cold and again with no change, on both paths
warnings-b witness_program_warnings — the cli's check on both paths, and the cases under tools/program-warnings/
warnings-c witness_program_warnings — the cli edited, built warm on the program layer
edit-a     witness_program_edit, WITNESS_ONLY="embed infer composed gathered"
edit-b     witness_program_edit, WITNESS_ONLY=1
edit-c     witness_program_edit, WITNESS_ONLY=5
edit-d     witness_program_edit, WITNESS_ONLY=10
edit-e     witness_program_edit, WITNESS_ONLY=rename
edit-f     witness_program_edit, WITNESS_ONLY=modes-whole
edit-g     witness_program_edit, WITNESS_ONLY=modes-layered
EOF
}

# whether build/avra was built from this tree's compiler source: the stamp's hash of that source, the
# commit it stood at aside — a commit that moves no compiler source moves no compiler
compiler_stands() {
    [ -x build/avra ] && [ "$(cut -d' ' -f1 build/.avra-built-from 2>/dev/null)" = "$(sh tools/work built-from . | cut -d' ' -f1)" ]
}

# what a built tree holds that a fresh one needs to stand as built: the compiler, its hot leaves, its
# stamp, and every object, archive, library, content stamp and dependency list build/ keeps at its top
packed() {
    for f in build/avra build/avra_hot.bc build/avra_hot.inc build/.avra-built-from; do [ ! -f "$f" ] || echo "$f"; done
    find build -maxdepth 1 -type f \( -name '*.o' -o -name '*.a' -o -name '*.so' -o -name '*.sha' -o -name '*.d' \) | sort
}

# a tree seeded from the pack `$1`, or left as it was: a pack is proved whole first — gzip's own check,
# a listing to its end, the compiler and its stamp in it — and refused when its stamp is not this
# tree's compiler source; then laid down in a staging directory and moved into build/ only once every
# file is out, so a truncated pack never seeds half a tree. Every file moved is touched to one instant,
# so make finds no object older than its own stamp — the content stamps decide what moved.
unpacked() {
    [ -f "${1:-}" ] || { echo "gate: unpack names a pack — sh tools/gate.sh unpack <file>" >&2; exit 2; }
    pack=$(cd "$(dirname "$1")" && pwd)/$(basename "$1")
    refused() { echo "gate: $(basename "$pack") $1 — not seeded" >&2; exit 1; }
    gzip -t "$pack" 2>/dev/null || refused "is not whole (gzip -t)"
    list=$(tar -tzf "$pack" 2>/dev/null) || refused "does not list to its end"
    for f in build/avra build/.avra-built-from; do printf '%s\n' "$list" | grep -qx "$f" || refused "holds no $f"; done
    packed_hash=$(tar -xzOf "$pack" build/.avra-built-from | cut -d' ' -f1)
    tree_hash=$(sh tools/work built-from . | cut -d' ' -f1)
    [ "$packed_hash" = "$tree_hash" ] || refused "was built from compiler source $packed_hash, this tree's is $tree_hash"
    stage=build/gate/unpacking
    mkdir -p build/gate
    [ ! -e "$stage" ] || find "$stage" -delete
    mkdir -p "$stage"
    if ! tar -xzf "$pack" -C "$stage"; then find "$stage" -delete; refused "did not extract"; fi
    touch build/gate/.unpacked
    printf '%s\n' "$list" | while IFS= read -r f; do
        [ -f "$stage/$f" ] || continue
        touch -r build/gate/.unpacked "$stage/$f"
        mv -f "$stage/$f" "$f"
    done
    find "$stage" -delete
    compiler_stands || { echo "gate: build/avra does not stand as HEAD's compiler after the unpack" >&2; exit 1; }
    echo "gate: seeded from $(basename "$pack") — build/avra stands as HEAD's compiler"
    exit 0
}

[ $# -ge 1 ] || { echo "gate: name a slice, or \`list\`" >&2; exit 2; }
slice=$1
shift
if [ "$slice" = list ]; then slices; exit 0; fi
if [ "$slice" = unpack ]; then unpacked "$@"; fi
[ "$slice" = seed ] && slice=pack
[ "$slice" = pack ] || slices | awk '{ print $1 }' | grep -qx "$slice" || { echo "gate: no slice \`$slice\` — \`sh tools/gate.sh list\` names them" >&2; exit 2; }

sha8=$(git rev-parse --short=8 HEAD)
out="$root/build/gate/$slice"
mkdir -p "$out"
find "$out" -mindepth 1 -delete
export AVRA_CACHE_DIR="$out/machine"
# a slice copies, counts and empties stores between builds, so each build saves its own before it
# answers; the build slice's timing rows alone leave the save to an heir, as a user's build does
export AVRA_STORE_KEPT_HERE=1
mkdir -p "$AVRA_CACHE_DIR"
began=$(date +%s)
rows=0
failed=0
failures=""

# one row: `$1` its name, the rest its command, bounded; its words at $out/<name>.log
row() {
    name=$1; shift
    rows=$((rows + 1))
    t0=$(date +%s)
    if sh tools/bounded.sh "$ROW_SECS" "$@" >"$out/$name.log" 2>&1; then
        echo "row $name pass $(( $(date +%s) - t0 ))s" >>"$out/rows"
        return 0
    fi
    failed=$((failed + 1))
    failures="$failures $name"
    echo "row $name FAIL $(( $(date +%s) - t0 ))s" >>"$out/rows"
    return 1
}

# a row that judges what an earlier row left: `$1` its name, `$2` the verdict (0 holds)
judged() {
    rows=$((rows + 1))
    if [ "$2" = 0 ]; then echo "row $1 pass" >>"$out/rows"; return 0; fi
    failed=$((failed + 1))
    failures="$failures $1"
    echo "row $1 FAIL" >>"$out/rows"
    return 1
}

# a row that compares against the old path: run only while the old path stands
old_row() { [ "$OLD_PATH" = 1 ] || return 0; row "$@"; }

# every store under the packages named emptied — a nested package's and a program test's too — so the
# rows after read them cold
cold() { for p in "$@"; do find "packages/$p" -name .avra-cache -prune -exec find {} -delete \; ; done; return 0; }

# build/avra as HEAD's compiler: kept when it was built from this tree's compiler source, else made in
# ONE generation — from the committed seed's link where no compiler stands, else from the one that does
# — with the package libraries beside it, built without building the compiler again. A gate's
# compiler makes no claim of the net, so it is built without it; the two-generation fixed point is the
# build slice's.
compiler() {
    if compiler_stands; then return 0; fi
    if [ ! -x build/avra ]; then row compiler-recover make recover || return 1; fi
    row compiler-gen1 env AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 make avra || return 1
    row compiler-libs env AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 make -o avra libs
}

# what `$1`'s cold build of packages/cli took, in seconds, net on or off by `$2`
cli_built() {
    cold cli
    find "$AVRA_CACHE_DIR" -mindepth 1 -delete
    c0=$(date +%s)
    row "cli-build-$1-cold" env -u AVRA_STORE_KEPT_HERE AVRA_PROGRAM_NET="$2" build/avra build packages/cli || return 1
    c1=$(date +%s)
    row "cli-build-$1-warm" env -u AVRA_STORE_KEPT_HERE AVRA_PROGRAM_NET="$2" build/avra build packages/cli || return 1
    echo "cli build net $1: cold $((c1 - c0))s, warm $(( $(date +%s) - c1 ))s" >>"$out/seconds"
    # the warm build's heir waited out, before a row after empties the store it saves
    env AVRA_PROGRAM_NET="$2" build/avra build packages/cli >/dev/null 2>&1 || :
}

slice_build() {
    row try make try
    row avra-a make avra && cp build/avra "$out/avra-a"
    cold cli
    row avra-b make avra && { cmp -s build/avra "$out/avra-a"; judged fixed-point $?; }
    cli_built on 1
    cli_built off 0
    judged cli-build-false-refusals "$(cat "$out"/cli-build-*.log | grep -c 'program-layer false refusal')"
}

# the std-avrac suite over `$@`, its paths under the package: one row for every path of std-avrac's
# own, and a row each for a path that is a package of its own nested in it, which `test` proves apart
avrac() {
    cold std-avrac
    own=""
    for p in "$@"; do
        if [ -f "$p/avra.toml" ]; then tested "std-avrac-$(basename "$p")" "$p"; else own="$own $p"; fi
    done
    [ -z "$own" ] || tested std-avrac $own
}
# half of std-avrac's src/compiler/tests, the `$1`-th (from 0), dealt in turn
compiler_tests_half() { find packages/std-avrac/src/compiler/tests -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 ! -name '.*' | sort | dealt "$1" 2; }
slice_avrac_a() {
    avrac $(
        {
            compiler_tests_half 0
            find packages/std-avrac/src/compiler -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 ! -name tests ! -name soundness ! -name '.*'
        } | sort
    )
}
slice_avrac_g() { avrac $({ compiler_tests_half 1; echo packages/std-avrac/src/compiler/soundness; } | sort); }
slice_avrac_b() { avrac $(find packages/std-avrac/src/features -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -type d -name '[a-e]*' | sort); }
slice_avrac_c() { avrac $(find packages/std-avrac/src/features -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -type d -name '[f-m]*' | sort); }
slice_avrac_d() { avrac $(find packages/std-avrac/src/features -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -type d -name '[n-r]*' | sort); }
slice_avrac_e() { avrac $(find packages/std-avrac/src/features -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -type d -name '[s-z]*' | sort); }
slice_avrac_f() {
    avrac $(
        {
            find packages/std-avrac/src/features -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -name '*.av'
            find packages/std-avrac/src -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 ! -name compiler ! -name features ! -name '.*'
        } | sort
    )
}

# the words on its lines that `dealt k n` keeps: every n-th, starting at the k-th (from 0), so a
# list's parts share its weight in turn
dealt() { awk -v k="$1" -v n="$2" '(NR - 1) % n == k'; }

# `test` over `$2…` as the row `$1`, judged by the NAMES that fail: each must be one
# tools/gate/<package>.names pins (a case a sandbox's environment fails — root writes any directory, no
# terminal, no network), never a count. With no pin file, every failure fails the row.
# A CASE THAT ENDS THE SUITE'S PROCESS (`avra: while running <case>`) fails no case by name and leaves
# every case after it unrun, so it is never passed over: each must be one tools/gate/<package>.traps
# lists, by the first line the runner says it under.
tested() {
    name=$1; shift
    pkg=$(echo "$1" | cut -d/ -f2)
    sh tools/bounded.sh "$ROW_SECS" build/avra test "$@" >"$out/$name.log" 2>&1
    ran=$?
    grep '^    ✗' "$out/$name.log" | sed 's/ @ .*//; s/^    ✗ //' | sort -u >"$out/$name.failed"
    listed "tools/gate/$pkg.names" >"$out/$name.known"
    comm -23 "$out/$name.failed" "$out/$name.known" >"$out/$name.unpinned"
    grep '^avra: while running ' "$out/$name.log" | sed 's/ @ .*//; s/^avra: while running //' | sort -u >"$out/$name.trapped"
    listed "tools/gate/$pkg.traps" >"$out/$name.traps"
    comm -23 "$out/$name.trapped" "$out/$name.traps" >"$out/$name.untrapped"
    if [ -s "$out/$name.untrapped" ]; then judged "$name" "$(wc -l <"$out/$name.untrapped" | tr -d ' ')"; return; fi
    # a run that fails no case and ends none must have exited clean; one that fails only pinned cases
    # or ends at a listed one stopped on them
    if [ ! -s "$out/$name.failed" ] && [ ! -s "$out/$name.trapped" ]; then judged "$name" "$ran"; return; fi
    judged "$name" "$(wc -l <"$out/$name.unpinned" | tr -d ' ')"
}

# the lines the pin file `$1` lists, sorted, each once; none where there is no such file
listed() { if [ -f "$1" ]; then grep -v '^#' "$1" | sort -u; fi; }

# THE CLI'S SUITE RUNS WITH THE NET: its cases run build/avra as a user does and hold the words a user
# meets, refusals among them, and where the program layer accepts a program the old path refuses, those
# words are the net's — so the suite holds the shipped default, the net on. The one suite that runs the
# compiler as a child; every other test row holds what it runs in-process.
slice_cli() {
    cold cli
    export AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=1
    children_kept tested cli-suite packages/cli
    export AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0
    children_of_failed cli-suite
}

# A SUITE WHOSE CASES RUN THE COMPILER AS A CHILD KEEPS WHAT EACH CHILD DID: `$@` with every child
# `<tree>/avra` filed under $out/children/<case> by tools/gate/child_kept.sh — its arguments, its
# streams and its exit — so a red row has the words its children said.
children_kept() {
    find "$out/children" -delete 2>/dev/null || :
    export AVRA_BIN="$root/tools/gate/child_kept.sh" AVRA_CHILD_BIN="$root/build/avra" AVRA_CHILDREN="$out/children"
    "$@"
    unset AVRA_BIN AVRA_CHILD_BIN AVRA_CHILDREN
}

# the children of the cases row `$1` failed, kept; every other case's dropped
children_of_failed() {
    for d in "$out"/children/*/; do
        [ -f "$d/case" ] || continue
        grep -qxF "$(sed 's/ @ .*//' "$d/case")" "$out/$1.failed" || find "$d" -delete
    done
}

slice_program() {
    cold std-program std-relation
    tested std-program packages/std-program
    tested std-relation packages/std-relation
    row runtime-tests make runtime-tests
    # THE ROWS' CLAIMS, generated from rt_sigs(): the C header and the typed methods. A row added without
    # its regeneration is refused here, never left for the next lane to find.
    row rt-header make rt-header
    row rt-ns make rt-ns
}

# each package the diff from the base sha `$1` touches, whose name the pattern `$3` matches (`$2` keep)
# or doesn't (`$2` drop), checked against the baseline
idioms_on() {
    [ -n "${1:-}" ] || { echo "gate: $slice needs the base sha its diff starts at" >&2; exit 2; }
    if [ "$2" = drop ]; then pick=-vxE; else pick=-xE; fi
    for p in $(git diff --name-only "$1" HEAD -- packages | cut -d/ -f2 | sort -u | grep $pick "$3"); do
        [ -d "packages/$p/src" ] || continue
        cold "$p"
        row "idioms-$p" build/avra check "packages/$p" --baseline tools/idioms.baseline
    done
}

# every `.av` the diff from the base sha `$1` changes, canonical as the tree's own compiler prints it.
# The base is the program landed last: a batch gated against its own base would hold none of what
# its lanes wrote to the printer's word
fmt_on() {
    [ -n "${1:-}" ] || { echo "gate: $slice needs the base sha its diff starts at — the program landed last" >&2; exit 2; }
    row fmt-changed env AVRA=build/avra sh tools/fmt_changed.sh "$1" HEAD
}

slice_sound() {
    row sound-check-run env AVRA_SOUND_CHECK=1 build/avra check packages/cli
    cold cli
    row llvm-verified-build env AVRA_VERIFY_LLVM=1 build/avra build packages/cli
    judged sound-check-defects "$(grep -c 'language.defect' "$out/sound-check-run.log")"
}

# the census compiler builds from build/avra, the compiler this slice stands on
slice_cost() { row cost env CENSUS_BUILDER=build/avra make -s -o avra cost; }

doors() { for p in "$@"; do cold "$p"; tested "test-$p" "packages/$p"; done; }
slice_doors_a() { doors $DOORS_A; }
slice_doors_b() {
    doors $DOORS_B
    row ui-host-test make -s -o avra ui-host-test
    row ui-host make -s -o avra ui-host
}

# each package named: tapes --findings with no refusal; built — a library stops at "declares no entry
# point", which is no refusal — with no program-layer false refusal; the cli's builds are the build slice's
findings_on() {
    for p in "$@"; do
        cold "$p"
        row "findings-$p" build/avra tapes "$root/packages/$p" --findings
        judged "refusals-$p" "$(grep -c '^error\[' "$out/findings-$p.log")"
        [ "$p" != cli ] || continue
        sh tools/bounded.sh "$ROW_SECS" env AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=1 build/avra build "packages/$p" >"$out/build-$p.log" 2>&1
        judged "false-refusals-$p" "$(grep -c 'program-layer false refusal' "$out/build-$p.log")"
    done
}

# written in into the code it generates is built cold in one directory; then, its own store and the

# first directory's path would build a second binary naming it: the three binaries are the same

app="$R/one/app"

use @std.meta.{Declared, Type, beside, literal}

/// `@placed`: the type says where its first field was written.
export fn placed(t: Type) -> Declared {
    let file = t.fields.first()?.at?.file ?? "nowhere"
    Declared { made: [beside(t, quote { impl ${t} { static fn written_in() -> string { ${literal(file)} } } })] }
}

#!/bin/sh
# A BINARY IS A FUNCTION OF ITS PACKAGE, NOT OF WHERE THE TREE STANDS. One
# package, a generic instantiated twice, built at two depths: no symbol may
# carry the building machine's path, so the two binaries are the same bytes.
set -u
. "$(dirname "$0")/lib/attack.sh"
R=build/moved-tree-attack
rm -rf "$R" && mkdir -p $R/one $R/two/deeper
for d in $R/one/app $R/two/deeper/app; do
    mkdir -p $d/src/a
    printf '[package]\nname = "moved-tree-attack"\nversion = "0.1.0"\n' > $d/avra.toml
    printf 'export fn id<T>(x: T) -> T { x }\n' > $d/src/a/k.av
    printf 'use a.{id}\n\nprintln("${id(3)} ${id("s")}")\n' > $d/src/main.av
    ./avra build $d > $R/out 2> $R/err || { fail "$d did not build: $(head -2 $R/err | tr '\n' ' ')"; continue; }
    got=$($d/src/main 2>&1)
    [ "$got" = "3 s" ] || fail "$d printed '$got', wanted '3 s'"
    cp $d/src/main $d.bin
    # a signature is made where the binary was signed; the code it signs is what is compared
    command -v codesign > /dev/null && codesign --remove-signature $d.bin
done
if [ $fails -eq 0 ]; then
    n=$(cmp -l $R/one/app.bin $R/two/deeper/app.bin 2>&1 | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
    [ "$n" = 0 ] || fail "the binaries built at two depths differ in $n byte(s)"
fi
verdict "moved-tree-attack" "one package built at two depths"

Built over a store that came from another tree, a gen-1 embeds 13 ABSOLUTE paths (/work/avra/packages/std-avrac/src/core/{nodes,expr/expr,stmt/stmt,pat/pat}.av and grammar/node files: expr_spine, components, closures, tasks, select_expr, grammar_lit), where a cold build writes `{tree}/…`. So some stored answer keeps an absolute path where a fresh one writes `{tree}`. The law: an answer holds only tree-relative places, so the same answer is the same bytes in any tree. Find the family that stores the absolute path (an attack: build over a store copied from another directory, then cmp against cold), fix it at the one door that writes places, and add the attack as a witness-b row. This also matters for your prebuilt std answers: an installed toolchain's paths differ from the build machine's.

<stdin>:18: SyntaxWarning: invalid escape sequence '\;'
set -u
[ $# -ge 3 ] || { sed -n 2,10p "$0"; exit 2; }
avra=$1; std=$2; out=$3
shift 3
named="$*"
# the compiler's own packages, never a program's import
COMPILERS=" std-avrac std-http-fuzz std-http-soak std-ui_gallery "
[ -x "$avra" ] || { echo "std_answers: no compiler at $avra" >&2; exit 1; }
[ -d "$std" ] || { echo "std_answers: no std at $std" >&2; exit 1; }
scratch=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'find "$scratch" -delete' EXIT
mkdir -p "$out"
find "$out" -mindepth 1 -delete
n=0
for p in "$std"/std-*; do
    [ -f "$p/avra.toml" ] || continue
    if [ -n "$named" ]; then
        case " $named " in *" $(basename "$p") "*) ;; *) continue ;; esac
    else
        case "$COMPILERS" in *" $(basename "$p") "*) continue ;; esac
    fi
    # the verdict: the package's own check, its answers kept apart and let go
    AVRA_CACHE_DIR="$scratch" AVRA_MACHINE_STORE_DIR="$scratch/judged" AVRA_VERDICT_DIR="$out" AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 "$avra" check "$p" >/dev/null 2>"$scratch/said" ||
        { echo "std_answers: $(basename "$p") is refused by its own compiler:" >&2; cat "$scratch/said" >&2; exit 1; }
    # the answers: what a program over the package reads of it
    AVRA_CACHE_DIR="$scratch" AVRA_MACHINE_STORE_DIR="$out" AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 "$avra" cache dependents "$p" >/dev/null 2>"$scratch/said" ||
        { echo "std_answers: what a program reads of $(basename "$p") was not worked out:" >&2; cat "$scratch/said" >&2; exit 1; }
    find "$p" -name .avra-cache -type d -prune -exec find {} -delete \;
    n=$((n + 1))
done
find "$out" -mindepth 1 ! -name 'pack-*' ! -name 'verdict-*' -delete
echo "std answers: $n packages, $(ls "$out" | wc -l | tr -d ' ') packs, $(du -sk "$out" | cut -f1) KB in $out"

Lead: approved, A then B, exactly as written.
A: a check reports warnings, rule findings and stale citations for the CHECKED package only. A dependency's own are `avra check <dep>`'s business. Say it once in the check's summary line when a dependency's warnings were not judged, e.g. "dependencies' warnings are theirs: `avra check <dep>`", so it's visible magic, not silence.
B: a path dependency's refusals are judged as today. An unedited toolchain std package stands on its install verdict, held to its file digests; an edited one is judged like a path dependency. Add an attack for B: edit one installed std file to a type error, and the downstream check refuses it.
Flip the warnings witness's dependency cases with reasons. Then the size and the cold check after each, then (c).

<to_controller>(0) ANSWERED, by probing both paths. A path dependency carries each of the four kinds below; the app that depends on it is checked:
1. a rule warning (loops.push_loop): shown, exit 0, both paths;
2. a law warning (type.coalesce_never): shown, exit 0, both paths;
3. a stale `// LICENSED` id: **refuses, exit 1**, both paths;
4. a law error (type.mismatch): **refuses, exit 1**, both paths.

So today a dependency's findings DO reach the check's output and verdict, by design on both paths. The cost is real for std: a program that only does `use @std.http.{Request}` gets 4 warnings about std-http's and std-http_message's own code (type.alias_copy ×2, lists.bool_comprehension_range, type.coalesce_never; the old path says 3). The user can't act on them.

What the user needs, and why:
- (i) ERRORS in a dependency: needed for a PATH dependency (the user's own code; a build over it must refuse, and check says why). For the TOOLCHAIN's std they can't happen: std is checked clean at install (std_answers.sh fails install otherwise) and is immutable unless edited.
- (ii) WARNINGS, rule findings and stale citations in a dependency: the user can't act on them in std. For a path dependency, `avra check <dep>` is where they belong. Rust does this (`--cap-lints` for dependencies).

Proposal for the cut:
- A. A check judges warnings, rules and stale citations of the CHECKED package only. That removes the rule families (file_rule_rows, item_fact_found, item_syntax_found, item_alone …), stale_citations and the warning laws from a downstream check, and from what ships. It is a behaviour change on BOTH paths, so the warnings witness's dependency cases flip and the old path gets the same scope.
- B. A dependency's refusals are judged for path dependencies. For the toolchain's std, the install's clean verdict stands in, held to the std files' digests: an unedited std package gets no law asks at all, and an edited one is judged like a path dependency. That drops the 21 law families from what ships for unedited std.

Together these should leave the shipped pack mostly tapes, names and typing, which a build needs. I'll measure the cold check and the size after each, and then do (c). A is a user-visible change (fewer warnings). OK to do A, then B?</to_controller>

I answered the lead's question (0) and stopped there: the cut it leads to changes what users see, so I've asked before building it.

**Answer to (0):** a dependency's findings do reach a downstream `check`'s output, verdict and exit code, on both the old path and the program layer. I checked an app that depends on a path dependency, adding four kinds of finding to the dependency one at a time:

| Finding in the dependency | What the app's `check` does (both paths) |
|---|---|
| rule warning (`loops.push_loop`) | shows it, exit 0 |
| law warning (`type.coalesce_never`) | shows it, exit 0 |
| stale `// LICENSED` id | refuses, exit 1 |
| law error (`type.mismatch`) | refuses, exit 1 |

This hurts users of std. A program whose only line is `use @std.http.{Request}` gets 4 warnings about std-http's and std-http_message's own code (the old path shows 3), and the user can't fix any of them.

**What the user actually needs:**
- **Errors in a path dependency:** yes. That's the user's own code, and a build over it fails anyway, so `check` should say why.
- **Errors in the toolchain's std:** these can't happen unless someone edits std. Install already refuses a std that doesn't check clean.
- **Warnings, rule findings and stale citations in any dependency:** no. They belong to `avra check <dependency>`. Rust does the same with `--cap-lints` for dependencies.

**Proposed cut:**
- **A.** A check reports warnings, rule findings and stale citations for the checked package only. That removes the rule families, the warning laws and the stale-citation query from a downstream check, and from what ships. It changes what users see on both paths, so the warnings witness's dependency cases will flip.
- **B.** Errors are still judged for path dependencies. For an unedited toolchain std, the install's clean verdict stands in, checked against the std files' digests, so it gets no law asks at all. An edited std package is judged like a path dependency. This drops the 21 per-item law families from what ships.

After each step I'll measure the cold check time and the shipped size. Then comes (c): storing each read as an index into a per-pack table, not as repeated hashes.

**Waiting on:** the lead's OK to do A, then B.

message.content:
Lead: before (b) or (c), ask the question your trace raises. Why does a downstream check run law and rule families over a DEPENDENCY's items at all? A user's check reports findings in the user's files. If std-json's laws can never surface in a downstream check, then asking item_fact_found, item_alone, the 21 law families and the rules for 319 json items is pure waste on every cold check, not just shipped bytes. Not asking them makes the cold check faster and makes those families unneeded in the shipped pack in one move.
So:
(0) check whether any law or rule finding in a dependency reaches a downstream check's output, or changes its verdict or exit code. If none do, a dependency's items get no law asks, and that's the first cut; measure the cold check and the shipped size after it. If some do, name which, and why the user needs them.
Then (c), dictionary-indexed reads in the pack format, since it's general and you own the store. (b), fusing the law families, belongs to laws-fusion (it has done the fold before); I'll hand it to them if (0) doesn't already remove those families from what ships. (d) not now.

<to_controller>CORRECTION to the breakdown, point 4(a): a downstream CHECK, now traced, asks the check-time families for its whole closure too (item_fact_found / item_alone / item_syntax_found for all 319 of json's items; file_rule_rows / stale_citations for its 9 files). The old check also ran rules over every program file. So only **18 families, 18 MB**, are never asked by a build or a check; (a) is worth −18 MB, not −90. The size has to come from (b) fusing the 21 per-item law families (≈ −200 MB of records over empty answers) and (c) dictionary-indexed reads in the pack format (the general fix; xz 6.3× shows the redundancy), or (d) gzip for shipping only. My order: (b), then (c). Waiting for your call before cutting. Committed meanwhile: 80666390 (the exclusion, `avra cache families`, AVRA_QUERY_FAMILIES) and 4c9e6447 (check reports its families too).</to_controller>

I've measured where the shipped std answers' bytes go, and I'm waiting on the lead's choice of what to cut before changing anything.

**Size after leaving out the compiler's own packages:** 626 MB, down from 1.09 GB. That covers 41 packages and 137 kinds of saved answer ("families").

**Where the bytes go:**
- **Dependency records, not answers, are most of it.** 436 MB is the list of reads each saved answer depends on; the answers themselves are 154 MB.
- **The per-item checks are the biggest single cost.** 21 per-item law-check families save about 18,800 questions each, with empty answers but 214 MB of records.
- **The rest:**
  - tapes and items: 119 MB
  - names, scopes and typing: 107 MB
  - generation and lowering: 45 MB
  - everything else: 103 MB

**What a downstream program reads:** I traced a cold `build` and a cold `check` of a program using `@std.json`. Each reads only its own closure: 319 of the 18,832 std items, about 2%.
- Checking a saved answer means checking every read under it, so anything inside an imported closure gets read. Savings have to come from whole families, not from individual items.
- A downstream `check` also runs the rule and law checks over its dependencies' files, as the old check did. So only 18 families (18 MB) are never asked for. I first told the lead 90 MB from the build trace alone, then corrected it.

**Options to get under 100 MB**, all sent to the lead:
- **(a) Drop the never-asked families:** −18 MB.
- **(b) Merge the 21 per-item law families into one per-item query:** about −200 MB, and it shrinks every user's own store too.
- **(c) Store each read as an index into a per-pack table of hashes**, instead of repeating 16-byte hashes. xz compresses a pack 6.3× and gzip 3.1×, which shows how much repetition there is. This is a store format change and the biggest general win.
- **(d) Ship the answers gzip-compressed and unpack at first use:** shrinks the download only, not the space used on the user's disk.

I recommended (b) then (c), each re-measured to keep the same cold-build times.

**Committed, no cuts:**
- **80666390:** std answers leave out std-avrac, std-http-fuzz, std-http-soak and std-ui_gallery. It also adds `avra cache families [<store>]` (bytes per family) and `AVRA_QUERY_FAMILIES=1` (every family a run asked for).
- **4c9e6447:** `check` reports its families the same way `build` does.

I haven't run the gate on these two commits, and the bundle in `/work` still ends at 2e56e49f.
